# Reference values captured from the real Lua `game/transport/fake_relay.lua`
# (plus `game/transport/contract.lua`, `game/transport/fake_star.lua`, and
# `game/online/input_protocol.lua` for the wire-cost scenario). This vector
# is frozen and cannot be regenerated: the Lua implementation it was
# captured from no longer exists in this repository. A failing differential
# against it is a finding about the Rust or TypeScript code under test, not
# a fixture to refresh. See tools/lua_reference/README.md for provenance.
# See `crates/gc-netcode/tests/fake_relay.rs` for the consumer and the exact
# Rust-side reproduction of each scenario.
#
# 1. `ENCODE_ADDRESSED_*_HEX` / `DECODE_*` — `contract.encode_addressed`'s
#    exact wire bytes for a control message whose payload needs
#    percent-escaping (space, `|`, `%`, `\n`) and for an input message with a
#    tick, plus `contract.decode_addressed` round-tripping the control wire
#    back into its fields. Exercises `fake_relay::encode_addressed`/
#    `decode_addressed`/`escape`/`unescape` — the one part of this port with
#    no `crate::fake_star` analog, since a star never round-trips a message
#    through text.
#
# 2. `DRAIN_ORDER` — a 3-member room; `guest_1` sends three control envelopes
#    and `guest_2` sends two input envelopes to `host`, interleaved, then the
#    room is pumped once and `host` drains with `poll()` (not `poll_batch`)
#    one entry at a time. Pins the exact persistent (slot, channel-rank)
#    cursor order `fake_relay::take` computes — round-robin over 2 slots x 2
#    channels, control ranked before input, skipping empty (slot, channel)
#    pairs within one `poll()` call.
#
# 3. `BACKPRESSURE_*` — a fresh 3-member room, host `buffered_amount_limit =
#    25`, broadcasting four 10-byte-payload input envelopes to both guests.
#    Each 23-byte envelope exceeds the 25-byte budget after the first, so
#    backpressure latches once per flush pass; this exercises the property
#    that is the whole point of a relay's shared uplink — the budget is
#    charged **once** per broadcast unit, not once per target, unlike
#    `fake_star`. `BACKPRESSURE_FINAL_UPLINK_UNITS`/`_BYTES` are cumulative
#    since construction (envelope count/bytes put on the uplink, unaffected
#    by how many pumps it took to drain).
#
# 4. `OVERFLOW_*` — a fresh 2-member room, `queue_limit = 2`, five control
#    sends to the same peer: two accepted, three rejected once the shared
#    uplink queue is full. `OVERFLOW_DIAGNOSTICS_OVERFLOW_COUNT=7` looks
#    surprising for three overflow sends — it is real Lua behaviour, not a
#    capture error: `event_limit = max(2, queue_limit) = 2`, and
#    construction alone (`initialize` on both sides, each pushing a
#    `peer_state` event) already evicts one event before any send happens
#    (+1). Each of the three failed sends then contributes *two* to the
#    counter: one from `_record_error`'s own `code == "overflow"` branch,
#    and a second from `_push_event`'s independent "the event queue itself
#    is full" branch, since the queue is already at its 2-event cap by the
#    time the first send fails. `1 + 3*2 = 7`. `fake_relay::record_error`/
#    `push_event` must reproduce this exact compounding, not merely "some
#    overflow got counted".
#
# 5. `WIRE_COST_<member>_*` — the `transport_relay_topology_probe_measures_sequencer_less_per_node_wire_cost`
#    scenario (8-member room, 60 ticks, one real encoded single-slot guest
#    bundle broadcast per member per tick), exact per-member integers rather
#    than the bracket `spec/game/transport_relay_spec.lua`/`tests/protocol.rs`
#    assert. Member 1 (`host`) receives from seven 7-byte-id `guest_N`
#    origins; members 2-8 receive from one 4-byte-id `host` origin plus six
#    7-byte-id origins, so `WIRE_COST_1_DOWNLINK_FRAMED_BYTES` is exactly
#    `3 * 60 = 180` bytes higher than every other member's — a real,
#    load-bearing check on per-line origin framing, not a rounding artifact.
#
# 6. `COMPARE_RELAY_*` / `COMPARE_STAR_UPLINK_BYTES` — one `broadcast` of a
#    213-byte input envelope (200-byte payload) across an 8-member relay
#    room versus the equivalent 7-guest star: `COMPARE_STAR_UPLINK_BYTES`
#    (1491) is exactly `COMPARE_RELAY_UPLINK_BYTES` (213) `* 7`, the
#    headline OMP-4 claim this whole module exists to measure.

ENCODE_ADDRESSED_CONTROL_HEX=686f73747c636f6e74726f6c7c317c6576656e747c377c7c68656c6c6f253230776f726c642537436e656564732532352532306573636170696e6725304168657265
